17 A combined heat and power (CHP) station generates electrical power and useful heat. The
diagram shows the input and output powers for a CHP station.
wasted power
60 MW
useful heating power
160 MW
input power
from fuel
useful electrical power
100 MW
What is the efficiency of the CHP station for producing useful power?
A
31%
B
38%
C
50%
D
81%

hints: List the three output arrows in the Sankey diagram: $60 \text{ MW}$ wasted, $160 \text{ MW}$ useful heating and $100 \text{ MW}$ useful electrical.
Recall that for CHP both heating and electrical outputs count as useful, so add $160 \text{ MW} + 100 \text{ MW}$ for the numerator.
Find the total fuel input power first by adding all three outputs, then use $\text{efficiency} = \text{useful output} / \text{total input}$.
walkthrough: Identify useful outputs from the diagram: useful heating power $=160 \text{ MW}$ and useful electrical power $=100 \text{ MW}$.
Add them for total useful power: $P_{useful} = 160 + 100 = 260 \text{ MW}$.
Use energy conservation to find total input: input must equal all outputs, so $P_{in} = 60 + 160 + 100 = 320 \text{ MW}$.
Calculate and convert to percent: $260/320 = 0.8125$, about $81\%$. This is option D.

A.explanation: This is $100/320$, the efficiency for useful electrical power alone, not for all useful power.

B.explanation: This compares $100 \text{ MW}$ electrical to $260 \text{ MW}$ useful, not useful output to total fuel input.

C.explanation: This is $160/320$, the efficiency for useful heating power alone, ignoring the $100 \text{ MW}$ electrical output.

D.explanation: Total useful power $160+100=260 \text{ MW}$ divided by total input $320 \text{ MW}$ gives about $81\%$.
